clue.text: Request fold in skirt to be trimmed

indicators.note: trimming cuts a bit off the end, so the last letter of the skirt word goes

parts.note: a pleat is a pressed fold in a skirt

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a pleat to be taken up in a skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be trimmed' takes the final T off PLEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an earnest appeal, a synonym of request.

clue.text: 1'I'm upset about a regulation in African country

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other here
in a down clue, upset turns the word I'm upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: taken as its letters, apostrophe dropped
a law is a regulation

explanation.surface: Someone is unhappy with a rule in an African state.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' reads upwards; 'about' signals the wrap, and 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked nation in south-east Africa.

clue.text: Descriptive image — drunken mother holding father up

indicators.note: holding means the reworked letters enclose the next piece
drunken means the letters of mother reel about into a new order
in a down clue, up means the father word is read bottom to top

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A tipsy mother hoists her father in a vivid picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' signals the anagram of mother, and 'up' reverses the father word, as a down clue is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A metaphor is a figure of speech that paints a picture by comparison.

clue.text: Emphasise tension

explanation.surface: Two words placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress is to emphasise, and stress is also strain or tension.

clue.text: Most of that I secure for Asian country

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter, so that loses its end

parts.note: to land something, as a catch or a deal, is to secure it

explanation.surface: Someone secures most of something for an Asian nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' means all but the last letter of that.
explanation.definitionFit: Thailand is a kingdom in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Consular changes involving one old Roman leader

indicators.note: involving means the shuffled letters take in the next pieces
changes says the letters of consular are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A consul changes, taking in an ancient Roman commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' shuffles the consular letters and 'involving' wraps them round one + old. Consular fits the surface: consuls were Roman magistrates.
explanation.definitionFit: Coriolanus was a legendary Roman general, subject of a Shakespeare tragedy.

clue.text: Insect a sprite repelled

indicators.note: repelled means pushed back, so the pair of words is read in reverse

parts.note: an elf is a sprite

explanation.surface: An insect drives off a fairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repelled' turns A + ELF round to give the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a small jumping parasitic insect.

clue.text: Shield invalid once he's cut

indicators.note: invalid means not sound, so these letters are taken apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: An invalid's shield once he has been wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invalid' looks like a sick person; it is the anagram signal on ONCE HE'S CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An escutcheon is the shield bearing a coat of arms in heraldry.

clue.text: Sport's blatant attempt to get positive comments?

parts.note: coarse means crude or blatant
fishing for compliments is angling for praise

explanation.surface: A sport described as a crude bid for praise.
explanation.walkthrough: COARSE FISHING is angling for freshwater fish other than salmon and trout, a common British pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse fishing is a branch of angling, a recreational sport.

clue.text: Country girl going behind prison

indicators.note: going behind means the girl's name follows the prison word

parts.note: can is slang for prison
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A country lass heads off behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going behind' puts the girl after the prison; 'Country' is a misleading adjective on girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is the North American nation north of the USA.

clue.text: Endless parties ruined if drink served early

indicators.note: ruined means the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order
endless means the last letter of parties is cut off

explanation.surface: Non-stop parties are spoiled if the drinks come out too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the S from PARTIES; 'ruined' shuffles PARTIE + IF.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal.

clue.text: Quits home, going into school?

indicators.note: going into means the home word is put inside the school word

parts.note: a school is a group of fish, hence fishes
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone leaves home to go to school.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags school as a shoal of fish, not a place of learning; 'going into' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit something is to end it, so a person who quits completes or stops it.

clue.text: One crashes liner-port wrecked around end of June

indicators.note: around means the reworked letters go round the next piece
wrecked means the letters of liner-port are smashed and reassembled
end of picks the last letter of June

explanation.surface: A liner wrecked off a port at the end of June.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' rearranges LINERPORT and 'around' takes in E, from 'end of June'.
explanation.definitionFit: An interloper intrudes uninvited, as a gatecrasher does.

clue.text: Food such as bread, no longer fresh — first of poor tucking in

indicators.note: tucking in means the letter goes inside the stale word

parts.note: stale means no longer fresh

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of poor

explanation.surface: Stale bread is eaten by the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking in' puts P, from 'first of poor', inside STALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is a basic everyday foodstuff, bread being a classic example.

clue.text: Keep attracting tourists to the capital

definitions.text: Keep attracting tourists to the capital

parts.words: Keep attracting tourists to the capital
parts.note: a keep is a castle's central tower; this one draws visitors in London

explanation.surface: Something that holds tourists in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' reads as a verb (keep attracting) but is the castle stronghold. The TOWER OF LONDON is a historic fortress on the Thames in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The fortress is famously a castle keep that draws crowds of sightseers in Britain's capital.

clue.text: Sudden good fortune giving a twist to autumn

parts.note: to wind is to twist or turn
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: A stroke of luck turns autumn around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A windfall is unexpected money or luck, literally fruit blown down.

clue.text: Block former schoolboy's attempt to depose King

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil, with the 's

indicators.note: depose means remove from power, so the King letter is thrown out

parts.note: to tackle something is to attempt it
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An old boy tries to overthrow the monarch but is blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, old boy, is British for a former pupil of a school; 'depose' removes the King.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle is something in the way, an obstruction.

clue.text: Expert not confused immediately

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert

indicators.note: confused means the letters of not are muddled

explanation.surface: An expert not confused gets on with it at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' turns NOT into NTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronto is informal for straight away.

clue.text: Criminal, freed, left with a wife

parts.note: out means freed, as from prison

explanation.surface: A criminal released, departing with his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlaw is a fugitive from the law.

clue.text: Like thriller writers, engaged in second employment

definitions.note: read as what is enjoyed in a thriller, a noun naming its appeal

indicators.note: engaged in means the writers are taken into the next word

parts.note: use is employment, as in the employment of a tool
pens are writers, things that write

explanation.surface: Thriller writers holding down a second job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like thriller' is read as the quality one likes in a thriller; 'engaged in' puts the writers into employment.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension and anxious uncertainty are what readers enjoy in a page-turner.

clue.text: Pass Gaudi article church recess

parts.note: el is the Spanish definite article, Gaudi being a Spanish architect
an apse is a vaulted recess at the end of a church

explanation.surface: A tourist moves past an alcove in one of Gaudi's churches.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaudi tells you the article is Spanish, and his famous church makes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses passes by.

clue.text: It creates litter in churchyards etc, if not regathered

indicators.note: regathered means the letters are collected up again in another order

explanation.surface: Wedding debris in churchyards, unless swept up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regathered' rearranges ETC + IF NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper scraps thrown over a bride and groom are left scattered round churches.

clue.text: Lack of interest, a route ending in unemployability

parts.note: a path is a route

indicators.note: ending in picks the final letter of unemployability

explanation.surface: Indifference on the way to being unemployable.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is indifference, a want of concern.

clue.text: Main body of craft in port

explanation.surface: Two definitions joined.
explanation.definitionFit: A hull is the main frame of a ship; Hull is also an English port on the Humber estuary.

clue.text: Biker with various challenges not about to take on learner driver

indicators.note: various means the letters are taken in assorted order
not here means without, so the about letter is struck out

parts.note: C is circa, about
L is the plate a learner driver displays

explanation.surface: A motorcyclist facing many tests refuses to take on a learner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not about' removes C from CHALLENGES; add L and 'various' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hells Angel is a member of a notorious motorcycle gang.

clue.text: Storage container very much filled with fuel, nothing less

indicators.note: filled with means the outer word holds the next piece

parts.note: so means very much, as in so tired

indicators.note: less means minus, so the nothing letter is subtracted

parts.note: oil is a fuel
O is nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A tank stocked with fuel, almost empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' subtracts nothing from the fuel, and 'filled with' places what remains inside very much.
explanation.definitionFit: A silo is a tower for storing grain or fodder.
